articles.title: Nasdaq 100 tumbles as Nvidia euphoria fades, new tariffs loom
articles.description: The technology-heavy gauge sank as much as 3%, and finished 2% lower — an about-face after the index surged almost 7% Monday on news of the surprise return of Jensen Huang to lead Nvidia Corp..

articles.title: Japan bond yield curve steepens as markets reassess BOJ rate hike path
articles.description: Japan's government bond yield curve steepened as investors reassessed the Bank of Japan's future interest rate outlook. Short-term yields declined on expectations of a lower terminal rate, while longer-term yields rose amid weak demand for 40-year bonds. Markets continue to anticipate a December rate hike to 1.5%.

articles.title: Trump Says It Is 'Not Too Late' For An US Equity Stake In Nvidia
articles.description: President Trump says it is "probably not too late" for the US government to take an equity stake in Nvidia, a day after Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO. He also said a pardon for Huang is "always an option," though he does not think one will be needed.

articles.title: Market timers get schooled with swings
articles.description: Investors face turmoil when navigating the stock market's unpredictable waves, especially after dramatic declines like last week's Nasdaq drop. Rapid recoveries can follow, but those who miss critical upward shifts often see their returns suffer. With growing market volatility, holding on to investments poses a challenge, and experts highlight that these sharp market swings tend to occur more frequently during downturns.

articles.title: Pledged gold worth less as prices crash 30%; gold loan NPAs nearly double
articles.description: India’s gold loan market recorded a doubling of non-performing asset (NPA) ratios in the first half of the fiscal year. Industry leaders have linked the increase to changes in lending regulations, saying borrowers are taking time to adapt to the revised norms. The central bank has directed gold loan financiers to collect interest through monthly installments for loans with tenures exceeding one year.

Audi India announces hike in vehicle prices by up to 2% from January 1
articles.description: German luxury carmaker Audi on Tuesday said it will increase ex-showroom prices of its models in India by up to 2 per cent with effect from January 1, 2027, to offset rising input costs. The latest hike marks Audi India's second price revision in 2026, as the automaker had previously raised prices by up to 2 per cent across its model range from April 1 this year. The price revision will be applicable across its model range, the company said in a statement. "In response to rising input costs, we will be implementing a price revision of up to 2 per cent. This adjustment is essential to maintaining the long-term sustainability of our business. We have kept this revision as measured as possible, and our focus remains on giving customers an ownership experience that solidifies their trust in the brand," Audi India Brand Director Balbir Singh Dhillon said.
